case_name: R. B. Subbaiyya v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

28 April 1969
Cr.A. No. 196 of 1965
The Judgment was delivered by: RAMASWAMI, J.
1.  This appeal is brought by a certificate under Art. 134(1)(c) of the Constitution from the judgment of the Patna High Court, dated 18 October, 1965, in Criminal Appeal No. 410 of 1963.
2. During the relevant period between 16 March, 1957 and 27 October, 1958, the appellant was working as District Engineer under the Southeastern Railway at Naomundi Banspani which is located in the district of Singhbhum. The charge against the appellant was that during the aforesaid period, he committed criminal misconduct in the discharge of his duties as a public servant and "obtained pecuniary advantage for himself
facts: The appellant was working as District Engineer under the Southeastern Railway at Naomundi Banspani which is located in the district of Singhbhum.

During the relevant period between 16 March, 1957 and 27 October, 1958, the appellant committed criminal misconduct in the discharge of his duties as a public servant and obtained pecuniary advantage for himself and others by giving contractors favourable rates in respect of earthwork done by them and by acquisition of assets worth more than Rs. 3 lakhs which were disproportionate to his known sources of income.

The charge against the appellant was that during the aforesaid period, he committed criminal misconduct in the discharge of his duties as a public servant and obtained pecuniary advantage for himself and others by giving contractors favourable rates in respect of earthwork done by them and by acquisition of assets worth more than Rs. 3 lakhs which were disproportionate to his known sources of income.
The specific charge levelled against the appellant was to taking illegal gratification from the contractors in the matter of classification of soils and of conspiracy with the contractors.
issues: Whether the trial Court was correct in holding that there was no satisfactory proof that the appellant classified the soils in the earthwork in a higher category than what it should have been and thereby made illegal gain to himself or the contractors.
Whether the presumption under S.5(3) of Act 2 of 1947 could be applied in this case.
petitioner_arguments: The contention put forward by the appellant is well-founded and must be accepted as correct.
The acquisitions were made out of family funds and the car was purchased out of the money which was given to him by his wife.
respondent_arguments: There was no direct evidence led on behalf of the prosecution to show that there was payment by any of the contractors to the appellant of any illegal gratification.
The High Court was not justified in differing from the trial Court on this point.
court_reasoning: In our opinion, the contention put forward by the appellant is well-founded and must be accepted as correct.

We are satisfied that the view taken by the trial Court is correct and the promissory note was held to be genuine and the payment of Rs. 91,000 in cash by Sripad Rao in January 1947 must be held to be established.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the conviction of the appellant for criminal misconduct under S.5(2) read with S.5(1)(a) to 5(1)(d) of Act 2 of 1947 is set aside.
The appellant is acquitted of the charges levelled against him.
